turns.question: In the declared-peer return-correlation network from December 2025 through March 12, 2026, which 10 pairs of stocks were the most strongly correlated, and did any pair move in opposite directions?

report.markdown:
**Top 10 strongest correlated stock pairs (Dec 2025 – Mar 12, 2026)**

| Rank | Pair | Correlation | Direction |
|------|------|-------------|-----------|
| 1 | GOOG – GOOGL | 0.9965 | Same direction |
| 2 | BRK.A – BRK.B | 0.9891 | Same direction |
| 3 | **BYNO – CEPO** | **‑0.9764** | **Opposite directions** |
| 4 | BF.A – BF.B | 0.9736 | Same direction |
| 5 | BELFA – BELFB | 0.9458 | Same direction |
| 6 | BATRA – BATRK | 0.9230 | Same direction |
| 7 | AUB – COLB | 0.9057 | Same direction |
| 8 | BEP – BEPC | 0.9016 | Same direction |
| 9 | CBRE – CWK | 0.9014 | Same direction |
| 10 | GS – MS | 0.8902 | Same direction |

**Yes, one pair moved in opposite directions.**
BYNO and CEPO had a correlation of **‑0.9764**, meaning their daily returns tended to move in opposite directions over the window. All other pairs in the top 10 were positively correlated (moved together).

turns.question: For the most strongly correlated pair in that result, compare the two stocks' returns and daily volatility over the same window.

report.markdown:
**GOOG and GOOGL had nearly identical losses and daily volatility** over December 1, 2025–March 12, 2026. [1]

| Stock | Window return | Daily volatility | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| GOOG | −5.308% | 1.399% | [1] |
| GOOGL | −5.268% | 1.404% | [1] |

GOOGL outperformed GOOG by just **0.040 percentage points**, while its daily volatility was slightly higher. Daily volatility is the standard deviation of daily returns, not annualized volatility. [1]

Returns run from the adjusted close before the window’s first session to the March 12 close. Both stocks had 70 session observations. [2]
